A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same Puppeteer research. Their complete main texts, equations, figures, tables and appendices are readable and support reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original humanoid-control experiments, ablations, gap-length generalization results and a 46-participant user study.

after.justification: v3 reports original control experiments, additional tracking and computational measurements, and a 51-participant user study.

M1.justification: The two TD-MPC2 world models, tracking pretraining, frozen low-level controller, termination loss and planning procedure remain unchanged. The original hyperparameter table is retained as Table 5. Fixed-frequency command execution is clarified rather than introduced as a different procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 836-clip MoCap dataset, eight tasks with the 56-DoF humanoid, and gap-length generalization scenario. Additional tracking measurements use existing data. The larger user study retains the same participant population and task coverage.

E2.justification: Figure 5 adds hierarchical SAC and DreamerV3 baselines using Puppeteer's low-level TD-MPC2 tracking agent on proprioceptive tasks. Figure 9 adds TD-MPC2 to the gap-generalization comparison. These materially expand the evaluated controls; MoCapAct and DeepMimic remain discussion-only comparisons.

E3.justification: Table 1 changes from training-averaged episode length on hurdles to episode length at 1M steps and convergence on gaps. Appendix B adds tracking evaluation with a 0.5 error threshold and 100-step truncation. v3 also reports best-of-tested-configuration SAC evaluation and increases user-study participation from 46 to 51.

E4.justification: The existing Figure 8 ablations remain. Appendix B extends tracking-data ablations with additional quality metrics and a 75% data condition; Figure 9 adds a baseline to the existing robustness analysis. Appendix D also reports unsuccessful SAC configuration trials. The qualitative cases are retained.

E5.justification: Reported seed counts increase from three to ten for Figure 5 and Table 1, substantially expanding replication of the main results while retaining confidence-interval and standard-deviation reporting. Figures 8 and 9 remain three-seed analyses. Appendix F newly discloses the two agent seeds used for user-study clip selection.

E6.justification: Learning curves are updated, and tracking, computational and additional baseline results are added. Table 1 replaces hurdles results with gaps results: Puppeteer versus TD-MPC2 survival is 115.9 versus 66.9 at 1M steps, but 159.3 versus 181.6 at convergence. These are not same-setting improvements over v1. Human preference updates from 97.6% to 97.8% with the larger study.

T1.justification: Appendices B and E add precise tracking-success definitions and explicit task-reward definitions, including previously unspecified velocity clipping and head-height terms. These are limited additions to mathematical specification; the MDP, model equations and termination loss remain unchanged, with no new theorem or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain stable. The introduction adds explicit claims of several-orders sample-efficiency advantages, absence of an equivalent benchmark, and no prior explicit evaluation of humanoid-policy naturalness. Section 3 removes the assertion that the approach requires no expert demonstrations.

C2.justification: v3 qualifies the reward-hacking interpretation as a conjecture, discusses SAC numerical instability and lack of planning as explanations for baseline failures, and explains retaining the upright reward term for fair comparison. The conclusion preserves the principal limitations but removes explicit manipulation examples and the source/target-task qualification on transfer.

D1.justification: v3 documents task rewards, action normalization, absence of image preprocessing, SAC configuration choices, and median-return clip selection from five rollouts per agent seed. Appendix C adds inference, memory and replay-storage details. The reproducibility statement newly announces checkpoint availability. These substantially expand disclosure without establishing changes to the retained Puppeteer implementation.

R1.justification: v3 sharpens the existing MoCapAct comparison with training-stage and interaction-budget details and expands discussion of adversarial motion priors and reusable skill encoders. References add AMP, ASE, newer humanoid-control work and REDQ, while SpawnNet is removed. The overall positioning as a reusable visual model-based hierarchy remains.

P1.justification: Most methodological prose and the six-section main narrative are retained. The introduction and related-work discussion are expanded, the conclusion is compressed, and ethics, reproducibility and acknowledgements paragraphs are added. Appendices are reorganized to accommodate the new material.

P2.justification: v3 adds three dedicated tables, expands Table 1 with separate early and converged survival columns, revises Figure 5 axes and legends, and adds the comparison curve to Figure 9. The ICLR template changes typography, headers and display placement. Existing qualitative images are reused and resized.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1's flat baselines and three-seed main results, v3 adds useful hierarchical controls and ten-seed estimates. Reward, clip-selection and resource disclosures also improve reproducibility. The gains are tempered by controls confined to proprioceptive tasks and stronger efficiency claims without matched direct comparisons. Incorrect human-preference percentages also persist in Section 4.2. Overall, the revision provides a positive but incremental quality improvement.
